references.text: Daniel's prophecy that the city and sanctuary will be destroyed, concerning "the abomination of desolation." Jesus links the siege of Jerusalem directly to the fulfillment of this prophecy of destruction ([ref:Dan 9:26-27|Daniel 9:26-27]).
Daniel prophesies about the desecration of the sanctuary and "the abomination of desolation," which Jesus connects to the coming destruction of Jerusalem ([ref:Dan 11:31|Daniel 11:31]).
Another reference in Daniel to "the abomination of desolation" being set up—a prophecy Jesus points back to in his discourse on the fall of Jerusalem ([ref:Dan 12:11|Daniel 12:11]).

Matthew's parallel account of Jesus' end-times speech. Where Luke mentions "Jerusalem surrounded by armies," Matthew uses the phrase "the abomination of desolation" standing in the holy place, with the same call to flee ([ref:Matt 24:15-16|Matthew 24:15-16]).

Mark's parallel account where Jesus warns about "the abomination of desolation" standing where it ought not, urging people to flee to the mountains—parallel to Luke's mention of armies surrounding Jerusalem ([ref:Mark 13:14|Mark 13:14]).

Earlier in Luke, Jesus weeps over Jerusalem and prophesies that enemies will build a ramp around the city, surround it, and level it to the ground—a direct prediction of what is described in 21:20 ([ref:Luk 19:43-44|Luke 19:43-44]).

Jeremiah prophesies about a scorching wind blowing against the daughter of Jerusalem—an image of the coming destruction of the city as punishment for the people's sin ([ref:Jer 4:11-12|Jeremiah 4:11-12]).

Moses warns that the Lord will bring a nation from afar to besiege all the cities in the land—a prophecy of siege pointing forward to the fall of Jerusalem ([ref:5 Mos 28:49-52|Deuteronomy 28:49-52]).
Isaiah prophesies that the Lord Himself will besiege Jerusalem and set up camps around it—a prophetic precursor to the destruction Jesus warns about ([ref:Jes 29:3-4|Isaiah 29:3-4]).

Jesus further explains that the siege of Jerusalem is the fulfillment of "the days of vengeance," when all that is written will come to pass—direct context for the verse about armies surrounding the city ([ref:Luk 21:22|Luke 21:22]).
